title.title: Stationary varifolds are regular almost everywhere
title.subtitle: Claim: every stationary integral $m$-varifold has $\mathcal{H}^m(\mathrm{Sing}\,V) = 0$, and in fact $\dim_H \mathrm{Sing}\,V \le m-1$

plain: Soap films may have creases where sheets meet, but the creases never take up any area

beats.text: Two crossing planes are stationary, singular along a set one dimension lower
Allard showed in 1972 the regular set is dense; multiplicity broke the rest
The claim: the singular set never has positive area, and the crossing is the worst case

steps: Zoom in at each point, keeping height and slope information
A unique-continuation step shows the zoomed picture is regular
So singular points are negligible: one dimension lower at most
